newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Dutch shares close at new record, U.S. data boosts.
newsitem.headline: Dutch shares close at new record, U.S. data boosts.

text.p: Dutch shares raced to a new record close after getting an extra boost from U.S. January unemployment data and a strong Wall Street opening.
The AEX share index ended just over one percent, or 7.03 points, higher at 694.25, surpassing its earlier record close of 689.95 points.

Dealers said the rally was not likely to end as recent data had given the market more confidence and some said several players remained short. "They had been expecting a correction after the recent gains, but that has not happened," said one.
The rising dollar throughout the session was also a motive for the bullish market.
Copier maker Oce-van der Grinten outperformed the market and dealers said this was partly due to the strong dollar.
"I've also heard some rumours about a possible takeover by Oce in the U.S.," said one dealer.
Other stocks that closed at a new record were Royal Dutch, Akzo Nobel, ABN AMRO, Fortis Amev, Nutricia, builder Ballast Nedam, Van Ommeren, Volker Stevin, Gist Brocades and Nutricia.
Nutricia called off talks with Friesland Dairy Foods, fuelling a rise in its shares by 8.70 guilders to 279.00.
Financials moved about in line with the market, with insurer Aegon outperforming as the stock was making up for some of the ground it had lost recently.
"Aegon looks expensive, but what is expensive nowadays," said one dealer.
Aegon performed well in January, but lost a little this week. It closed on Friday at 117.10 guilders, up 1.80 guilders, after hitting 120.30 guilders on January 28.
Vendex and Randstad were in demand as the outlook for temporary work sector in Germany and France looked good, analysts said.
Vendex, which announced it was buying shoe shop chain Scapino after the bourse closed, gained 3.10 guilders to 82.80.

Philips' shares moved from negative territory into the positive. The firm is to announce its 1996 results next Thursday and analysts expected a much lower profit from normal operations and added the firm could face a net loss in 1996.
Some dealers said the Philips share price was not too high but added it could dip a little after the release of the results next week. Philips gained 0.40 guilders to 74.80 on Friday.
